AccessPolicyEffect.description: What one access-policy statement does to the operations it names.

AccessPolicyScopeKind.description: Whose requests one access-policy statement covers.

preset.description:
Create an instance of a registered preset (ADR 0110): `shipright`,
`slack-adapter`, or `tidebreak`. The registry supplies kind, resource
family, capabilities, and the settings schema; the request supplies
the slug, the display name, and the service identity it mints for.
Omit for a custom add-on.

AddOnEnvironmentUpdateRequest.description:
Environment variables to write into or remove from a managed add-on's
workload. The plane holds the values write-only: a response names what is
set, never what it is set to.

unset.description: Variables to remove. A name the workload does not hold is ignored.

values.description:
Variables to set. A name already present is overwritten; every other
variable the workload holds is left alone.

AddOnHealthView.description:
Latest per-add-on reachability facts.

Three independent fact pairs — traffic success, traffic failure, probe —
each answering a different question; readers compare the timestamps to
decide which evidence is current. Gateway refusals never appear here.

last_failure_at.description: When authentication last failed in a way attributable to the add-on.

last_failure_status.description: HTTP status of that failure, when a response was received at all.

last_probe_at.description: When an admin probe last ran.

last_probe_detail.description:
Coarse probe classification (`http_<status>`, `dns`, `connect`,
`timeout`, `other`); never upstream prose.

last_probe_ok.description: Whether that probe got any HTTP response.

last_success_at.description: When a machine last authenticated successfully.

last_success_status.description: HTTP status of that success, when one exists.

AddOnHostingUpdateRequest.description:
Desired hosting state for one add-on (ADR 0095).

Writing it makes the row managed; every field is required because the
database's hosting-shape constraint takes the whole desired state or none
of it. The status trio is absent on purpose — the reconciler owns it. The
hostname override is the operator's bring-your-own name (ADR 0095
decision 4); a write that omits it clears it, so the row falls back to the
hostname the reconciler assigned — which no write here ever touches.

database_mode.description:
Where the workload's database comes from (ADR 0095 decision 5).
`none` — the add-on runs without a database — `external` — an
operator-supplied Secret — `gateway_schema` — a role and schema the
gateway provisions in its own PostgreSQL — and `colocated` — a
disposable PostgreSQL the plane runs beside the workload — are all
accepted.

egress.description:
Where the workload may speak beyond the gateway, cluster DNS, and
its database: `gateway` (the default) or `internet`, which adds
outbound HTTPS to public addresses.

image_digest.description:
Required for a pinned row: the one pin. Informational for a tracking
or first-party row — the reconciler owns the column and a write that
keeps what the row follows keeps the adopted digest — so a caller
echoing the view back need not strip it.

image_source.description:
`pinned` (the default), `track_release`, or `first_party` (ADR
0108): a first-party row follows the image this deployment pinned
for the add-on in `add_ons.hosting.first_party`.

release_hold.description:
Pauses adoption when true, on a tracking or first-party row; omitted
means following. Refused on a pinned row.

release_repository.description:
The GitHub repository (`owner/name`) a tracking row follows.
Required for `track_release`, refused otherwise.

release_soak_minutes.description:
The row's own soak window, in minutes from 0 through 10080. Only for
`track_release`; omitted takes the installation default.

source_sets.description:
Names of `add_ons.hosting.source_sets` entries restricting a public
add-on's ingress. Omit to leave a public add-on unrestricted; internal
exposure refuses the field, being already the private-ranges
restriction.

volume_mount_path.description:
The durable volume the plane owns for this workload (ADR 0095
decision 2, amended): mounted at `volume_mount_path`, sized
`volume_size` (a Kubernetes quantity such as `20Gi`), on an optional
`volume_storage_class`. Omit all three for no volume.

AddOnHostingView.description:
One add-on's hosting state (ADR 0095).

`mode` is always present; every other field is populated only on managed
rows, where the database's hosting-shape constraint guarantees the desired
state and the reconciler owns the status trio.

cluster_url.description:
The in-cluster origin another managed add-on reaches this workload at
(plain HTTP to its Service). Present while the row is installed. This
is how the Slack adapter is pointed at a hosted Tidebreak whose
Ingress is internal: the plane admits egress between managed add-ons,
and nothing else in the cluster resolves the private hostname.

egress.description:
`gateway` confines the workload to the gateway, cluster DNS, and its
database; `internet` additionally admits outbound HTTPS to public
addresses.

environment_digest.description:
Digest of the last environment write; the workload rolls when it
changes.

environment_keys.description:
Names of the variables written into the workload's environment Secret.
Names only: the plane holds the values write-only, so no path reads
them back.

image_digest.description:
The digest the workload converges toward. Absent only on a tracking
row that has not adopted a release yet.

image_source.description:
Where the digest comes from (ADR 0108): `pinned` — written with the
declaration; `track_release` — resolved by the reconciler from the
newest admitted release of `release_repository`; or `first_party` —
the image this deployment pinned for the add-on, adopted whenever a
deployment moves it.

oneOf.description:
The one-click hosting shape, present only for a first-party add-on
the gateway registers a preset for.

The verified build provenance of the running digest, when the trust
policy admitted it by provenance rather than by list (ADR 0108).

release_candidate_tag.description:
The newest release seen but not adopted, and why — soaking, not yet
published as an image, refused by the trust policy, or held.

release_checked_at.description: When the tracked repository's releases were last read.

release_hold.description: True pauses tracking: candidates are recorded, nothing is adopted.

release_repository.description: The GitHub repository (`owner/name`) a tracking row follows.

release_soak_minutes.description:
The row's own soak window in minutes; absent takes the installation
default.

release_tag.description: The release tag the running digest was adopted from, and when.

webhook_secret_digest.description:
SHA-256 hex of the minted webhook secret, when the row has one. A
digest, never the plaintext: the plaintext exists only in the mint
response and the workload's webhook Secret (ADR 0095 decision 5).

AddOnPairingReportResponse.description: What the gateway relays of an add-on's pairing report.

reachable.description:
Whether the add-on answered at all. `false` names the transport
failure in `detail`; the report itself may still say a machine is
unpaired while this is `true`.

report.description:
The add-on's own report, when it answered JSON. A 503 still carries
one: the adapter answers that way while a machine is unpaired.

target.description: Where the report was fetched from.

AddOnUpdateRequest.description:
Enablement is deliberately absent: the kill switch is its own audited
operation (`setAddOnEnabled`), matching every other admin surface.

client_id.description: The OAuth client identity tokens bind to. Stable across renames.

oneOf.description:
Latest reachability facts from machine authentication and admin
probes (ADR 0071 / 0094). Null means no evidence — never "healthy"
and never "broken".

preset.description:
The preset this row is an instance of (ADR 0110); null for a custom
add-on. The console groups by it.

AllowedAddOnImageView.description: One image trust policy entry (ADR 0095 decision 3).

digests.description:
Digests admitted from the repository by list. Empty on an entry that
admits by provenance.

oneOf.description:
The build a digest must prove to be admitted, on an entry that admits
by provenance (ADR 0108).

repository.description: Exact repository — registry host and path, with no tag and no digest.

ApiErrorBody.description: Error envelope, matching the shape the rest of the gateway returns.

fields.description: Per-field rule failures, present only for validation errors.

ApiErrorResponse.description: Response body for every non-success control-plane result.

apply_sequence.description:
Which application of this template this was, counting from one. It is
what suffixed the created names and engine keys.

ApplyGuardrailTemplateRequest.description:
The apply request.

It carries no `mode` and no `failure_stance`, and that is the mechanism
rather than an omission: apply always creates a monitor-mode, fail-open
policy, and `deny_unknown_fields` turns an attempt to ask for anything else
into a readable refusal instead of a silently ignored field (ADR 0066).

parameters.description: Declared parameter values, each a list of strings.

AuditEventListResponse.description: One page of the audit ledger.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page, or null at the end of the ledger.

actor.description: Who acted, as a label. Informational: never an authorization identity.

last_occurred_at.description: When it last recurred. Equal to `occurred_at` for a single occurrence.

metadata.description:
Content-free structured context, `{}` when the event carried none.

Non-secret request metadata only — e.g. the `client_id` and `scope` a
refused device-authorization request presented — never credentials or
request bodies.

occurred_at.description: When the action was first recorded, RFC 3339 in UTC.

occurrence_count.description:
How many occurrences this row represents.

Repeated identical actions collapse into one row rather than flooding
the ledger, so a count above 1 is a real repetition, not a duplicate.

target_id.description:
The specific object, when the action named one.

Null for an action against a class rather than an instance — a failed
sign-in has no object — and never a substitute for the identity in
`actor`.

target_type.description:
Kind of object the action concerned.

Here so a lifecycle event can be joined to the thing it happened to.
Without it a row saying a policy was disabled names no policy, and the
only way to find out which is to correlate timestamps against the
object listings.

AuditTargetKind.description: Resource category referenced by an administrative audit event.

AuthenticationPolicyAccounts.description: Account counts behind an authentication-policy decision.

local_only.description: Active accounts with a password and no enabled verified provider.

passwordless.description:
Active accounts holding no password at all.

Non-zero means withdrawing the last enabled verified provider is refused
with `sso_only_accounts`.

sso.description:
Active accounts linked to an enabled verified provider.

Population, not prediction: an account counted here may also hold a
password. See `passwordless` for the cohort a withdrawal is refused over.

AuthenticationPolicyView.description: The installation's sign-in policy and what it currently applies to.

accounts.description: Who the policy currently applies to.

login_mode.description: Which interactive sign-in methods are accepted.

updated_at.description: When the policy was last changed.

BedrockDataRetentionPolicy.description: Maximum data-retention mode accepted from Bedrock Mantle.

BillingClass.description: How the capacity that served an inference request is paid for.

reason.description:
Why the sandbox is being stopped, in a few words. Trimmed; at most 200
characters; recorded as `termination_detail` on the sandbox and in the
`administrator_cancelled` event.

CanonicalMismatchMemberView.description: One route whose canonical identity keeps it out of a group it belongs in.

gateway_id.description: Identifier clients request this route by; unchanged by the repair.

CanonicalMismatchView.description: Routes that look like one model but do not group as one.

members.description:
The routes whose canonical identity would change. Routes already
carrying the suggested value are not listed: nothing about them changes.

suggested_canonical_model_id.description: The canonical identity these routes would share once repaired.

ClientUsageView.description: Traffic grouped by the client that authenticated it.

attributed_requests.description:
Requests that resolved to a conversation, and so appear in conversation
views. The remainder routed successfully but asserted no conversation
identifier, which is why a working harness can look absent there.

avg_message_count.description: Mean northbound message count across committed requests that recorded one.

avg_tool_definition_count.description: Mean declared tool-definition count across committed requests that recorded one.

avg_user_message_count.description: Mean user-message count across committed requests that recorded one.

cache_savings_microusd.description:
Estimated metered spend prompt caching avoided, in micro-US-dollars.
Same contract as the by-user rollup: billed rows only, floored,
negative when write premiums exceeded read savings.

cache_write_input_tokens.description: Input tokens written to a provider prompt cache (cache writes).

cached_input_tokens.description: Cached (cache-read) input tokens on committed requests.

oneOf.description:
Client that minted the token, or null for rows recorded before clients
were identified.

first_turn_cache_write_input_tokens.description: Cache-write input tokens on committed first-turn requests.

first_turn_cost_microusd.description:
Estimated billed cost of committed first-turn requests, in
micro-US-dollars.

first_turn_input_tokens.description: Input tokens on committed first-turn requests.

first_turn_requests.description:
Committed first-turn requests: one user message and nothing else in
the transcript beyond the standing instructions block — the opening
request of a conversation, never a tool-loop continuation. What
starting a session costs — system prompt, standing instruction files,
and tool definitions land here with nothing yet amortized.

inference_requests.description: Requests from this client, including abandoned failovers.

last_activity_at.description:
Most recent request, so a silent client is distinguishable from one that
never connected.

peak_context_utilization.description: Peak input-tokens / context-window across committed requests.

priced_requests.description: How many of those requests carry a final price.

shape_recorded_requests.description:
Committed requests that recorded request-shape counts — the denominator
for the first-turn statistics. History that predates shape capture has
no `user_message_count` and is excluded from them, not counted as zero.

unattributed_requests.description:
Requests that resolved to no conversation — the same remainder, stated
as its own number so a reader reconciling conversation views against
this rollup does not have to derive it.

CloudIdentityMode.description: Cloud workload identity mode shown in provider summaries.

ConnectedAppAccessMode.description: Agent-facing interfaces enabled for one governed REST connected app.

operations.description:
Human-readable choices from the app's declared operation catalog.
Absent only when this app does not expose an enumerable catalog.

created_by.description: Administrator who created the statement; absent for seeded rows.

operation.description:
Exact operation identifier, `tool:<name>` on an MCP app, or `*` on a
deny.

scope_id.description: Scope instance, absent for app scope.

ConnectedAppAudience.description:
Population that may reach a connected app through a granted endpoint.

This gates *reachability* only. Every request still carries the calling
user's own authority, so widening the audience cannot widen what any
individual caller is permitted to do.

ConnectedAppAuthMethod.description: Credential mechanism used by a connected app.

ConnectedAppCaTrustView.description: What one app's egress trusts beyond the platform roots.

ca_trust_bundle.description:
The stored PEM, absent when none is configured.

Returned in full rather than as a presence bit, unlike every credential
on this app: a CA certificate is public material that the upstream hands
to any client that connects to it, so withholding it would protect
nothing and would stop an administrator checking what they pasted.

certificates.description: Each certificate the bundle asks this app's egress to trust.

configured.description: Whether a bundle is configured at all.

data.description: Apps visible on the caller's account surface and their personal status.

ConnectedAppConnectionView.description:
One connected app as it relates to the calling account.

These are presence and health facts only. No credential value, OAuth token,
client identifier, scope, or upstream account identity is returned.

available.description: Whether the app is enabled and the caller is currently granted it.

oauth.description: Whether this app connects the caller through OAuth.

oauth_connected.description: Whether the caller has an OAuth credential stored for this app.

oauth_expires_at.description: UTC expiry reported for the caller's OAuth access token, when known.

oauth_reauthorization_required.description: Whether that OAuth credential must be explicitly reauthorized.

personal_credential.description: Whether the caller has a user-owned static credential stored.

personal_credentials_allowed.description: Whether current policy allows the caller to attach a static credential.

ConnectedAppCredentialInput.description:
The credential the gateway will present to the app.

Which members are read depends on `kind` and `auth_method`; the ones that do
not apply must be absent. Every one of them is write-only — no operation
returns stored credential material, and `credential_configured` on the app
view reports only that something is stored.

github_app_private_key.description:
PEM-encoded RSA private key of the GitHub App a forge mints tokens from.

For `git_forge` apps whose `git_forge.credential_mode` is `github_app`,
and refused everywhere else. Optional even there: the console can create
the app on GitHub on the administrator's behalf, and the key it returns
does not exist until they have clicked through that. A forge configured
without one holds no credential and its egress is denied until it does.

Write-only, like every other member here. No operation in this document
reads a stored key back, and the app view reports only that one exists.

oneOf.description:
Which convention the login half of a basic forge credential follows.

Required for a `git_forge` app whose placement is `authorization_basic`.
Forges read meaning into the login: `x_access_token` injects the literal
`x-access-token` (GitHub App installation and fine-grained tokens),
`oauth2` injects the literal `oauth2` (GitLab-style OAuth tokens), and
`bot_user` injects the login supplied in `username`. Naming the
convention instead of typing the login is what keeps its meaning
machine-readable — `username` is refused alongside the two literal
conventions rather than silently discarded.

oauth_client_secret.description: OAuth client secret, for a `delegated_oauth` app whose issuer needs one.

oneOf.description: Which credential recipe is being supplied. Required for `datadog`.

shared_secret.description: The single secret a `shared_secret` app presents.

username.description:
Login half of a `git_forge` app's HTTP basic credential, for the
`bot_user` login convention only.

Its own field rather than a value guessed at injection time: a bot
account's login is something only the administrator knows. Encrypted
like every other component, which says nothing about it being secret.

ConnectedAppEffectiveAccessResponse.description: Effective access for one chosen principal.

ConnectedAppHealthView.description:
Latest per-app reachability facts (ADR 0069 D3, #1090).

Three independent fact pairs — traffic success, traffic failure, probe —
each answering a different question; readers compare the timestamps to
decide which evidence is current. Policy denials and per-user delegated
grant failures never appear here.

last_failure_at.description: When an exchange last failed in a way attributable to the app.

last_failure_status.description: HTTP status of that failure, when a response was received at all.

last_probe_at.description: When an admin probe last ran.

last_probe_detail.description:
Coarse probe classification (`http_<status>`, `dns`, `connect`,
`tls`, `timeout`, `other`); never upstream prose.

last_probe_ok.description: Whether that probe got any HTTP response.

last_success_at.description: When an upstream exchange last proved the integration alive.

data.description: Every connected app, deleted ones excluded.

ConnectedAppOauthInput.description: The delegated-OAuth client configuration a per-user grant is obtained with.

authorization_url.description: Authorization endpoint the user is sent to.

client_id.description: OAuth client identifier registered with the app.

discover.description:
Discover the upstream's authorization server and register a client
dynamically at create time (ADR 0069 D4). When set, the three manual
OAuth fields are left empty and filled by discovery; a server without
dynamic registration is refused with `oauth_registration_unsupported`
naming the manual path as the remedy.

scopes.description: Space-separated scopes requested for each user's grant.

token_url.description: Token endpoint the authorization code is exchanged at.

ConnectedAppOperationView.description: One operation an administrator can choose without knowing its internal key.

method.description: HTTP method for governed REST operations, when meaningful.

operation_id.description: Stable catalog key sent back when the operation is selected.

path.description: Path template for governed REST operations, when meaningful.

summary.description: Plain-language description supplied by the catalog, when present.

ConnectedAppView.description:
A connected app and the terms it is reachable on.

The bools are independent facts about one app — enabled, built in, and two
separate credential-presence bits — not a state machine. Each is read by a
different decision, and collapsing them into an enum would invent
combinations that do not exist while hiding the ones that do.

oneOf.description:
Which agent interfaces expose the app's buffered REST channel.

Null only for an app kind with no REST or git-forge projection.

allowed_model_ids.description: The allowed routes, empty when the mode is `all`.

audience.description: Who may reach the app. Meaningful only for the built-in app.

auth_method.description: How the gateway authenticates to it.

built_in.description: Whether the gateway provisions this app itself.

credential_configured.description: Whether a credential is actually present.

oneOf.description: Which credential recipe is stored, when one is.

enabled.description: Whether the app may be invoked at all.

oneOf.description:
Where a `git_forge` app's push credential comes from.

The three GitHub App fields below are non-secret configuration, not
credential material: an app id, the slug its pages are addressed by, and
the installation a token is minted for. The key that signs the mint is
never any part of this view — `credential_configured` reports its
presence and nothing reads it back.

git_forge_github_app_id.description: GitHub App a `github_app` forge mints from, once it has one.

git_forge_github_app_installation_id.description: Installation the forge mints for, once a human has approved one.

git_forge_github_app_last_minted_at.description:
When this gateway process last minted a token for the configured GitHub
App installation, if it has.

Per-process: minted tokens live in memory and are never stored, so a
replica that has not minted since it started reports nothing. Null is
"no evidence here", never "broken", and is also the ordinary value for
apps that are not GitHub App-backed git forges.

git_forge_github_app_slug.description: Slug that app's pages are addressed by, once it is known.

git_forge_has_intrinsic_rest_channel.description:
Whether this `git_forge` app carries the ADR 0052 intrinsic GitHub REST
channel (`github_app` mode and a stored OAuth client).

Distinct from `rest_tool_slug` / `rest_operation_count`, which the SPA
treats as "this is a REST app". The catalog ships with the kind; it is
not a `rest_api_connections` row.

git_forge_intrinsic_rest_operation_count.description: How many operations that channel exposes, when it is active.

oneOf.description:
Latest reachability facts from real traffic and admin probes
(ADR 0069 D3). Null means no evidence — never "healthy" and never
"broken"; a fresh app has nothing held against it.

model_access_mode.description: Which model routes may invoke the app.

oauth_client_configured.description:
Whether the app row holds an OAuth client the gateway can start a
per-user authorization with.

Not the installation credential `credential_configured` reports: that is
how the gateway authenticates itself, this is whether an individual user
can be sent through Connect to authorize on their own behalf. The two
are independent — a `github_app` forge has the first and, unless its
GitHub App conversion carried an OAuth client, not the second. That
conversion is the only writer and runs once, so a forge that completed
it without a client cannot grow one and has to be recreated. That is the
whole triage question, and it was previously unreadable.

A presence bit only. Neither the client id nor its secret is returned by
this or any other read.

oneOf.description:
How the app's OAuth client identity was obtained (ADR 0078).

The three paths leave an operator with different remedies:
`metadata_document` has nothing to rotate and nothing registered
anywhere, `dynamic_registration` may hold an expiring secret and a
management URI, and `manual` can only be edited here. Null means the
app holds no OAuth client at all.

oauth_client_secret_expires_at.description:
When the DCR-issued client secret expires, RFC 3339. Surfaced, never
auto-rotated; null when no expiry is known.

oauth_issuer.description:
Issuer a dynamically registered OAuth client belongs to (ADR 0069
D5); null for manually registered apps.

oauth_scopes.description:
Space-separated scopes sent on future authorization redirects. This is
non-secret configuration; existing grants keep their recorded scopes.

personal_credential_policy.description: Whether a caller's own credential may stand in for the installation's.

rest_operation_count.description: How many operations that projection exposes.

rest_tool_slug.description:
MCP tool slug of the governed REST projection, when there is one.

Non-null means this *is* a REST app. A `git_forge` app's intrinsic
GitHub REST channel does not populate this — see
`git_forge_has_intrinsic_rest_channel`.

ConversationCostEventView.description: One inference request within a conversation, with cost-debugging fields.

background_task_kind.description: Platform task kind when this is background model work.

batch_custom_id.description: Client-supplied item identifier within the Message Batch.

batch_id.description: Gateway-owned Message Batch identifier for an asynchronous item.

billing_class.description: How the serving capacity was paid for.

cached_input_price_microusd_per_million.description: Cache-read rate snapshot; null means the input rate applied.

context_window.description: Catalog context window of the serving route.

credential_class.description:
Credential class that produced this event: `user_subscription`,
`provider_api_key`, `workload_identity`, or `none`.

credential_resolution_reason.description:
Why resolution chose this credential (ADR 0027). Null when the provider
has no subscription dimension or the row predates the vocabulary.

fallback_from_subscription.description:
True when a subscription was attempted first and a metered credential
served instead.

finish_reason.description:
The provider's own finish or stop reason, raw and unnormalized. Null
means the provider reported none.

first_byte_ms.description: Time-to-first-byte in milliseconds, when an upstream response was observed.

gateway_model_id.description: Client-visible model ID, as recorded on the event itself.

input_price_microusd_per_million.description: Input rate snapshot used by this event's estimate.

message_count.description: Northbound turn items presented to the model.

model_id.description:
Catalog model, or null when the event predates model attribution or its
catalog row has since been deleted.

output_price_microusd_per_million.description: Output rate snapshot used by this event's estimate.

provider_name.description: Provider display name, as recorded on the event itself.

oneOf.description:
Proof that provisioned capacity served this successful request. Null
means the event carried no provider or route proof.

request_id.description:
The client-visible `x-request-id` this event was recorded under, when
one was captured. `getInferenceRequest` traces the same ID back to
this event.

subscription_binding_id.description:
The subscription binding this event drew on, or fell back from when
`fallback_from_subscription` is true. Null when none was involved.

subscription_label.description:
That binding's label, as shown on the account page. Null when the
binding has since been deleted or none was involved.

subscription_owner_email.description:
Email of the account that owns the binding; a teammate's under team
sharing (ADR 0037).

terminal_state.description:
How the upstream response ended: `completed`, `incomplete`, `truncated`,
or `failed`. Null means unrecorded — the event predates this vocabulary
or the path that served it reports no terminal state — and must not be
read as a completed response.

tool_call_count.description:
Tool or function call items the response carried. Null means uncounted,
which is distinct from a counted zero.

tool_definition_count.description: Declared tool/function definitions on the request.

ConversationHarness.description: Client family associated with an attributed model conversation.

ConversationListResponse.description: One page of the conversation listing.

data.description:
Conversations in the requested order; most recently active first by
default.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page, or null at the end of the listing.

Always null when `ranked` is true: a ranking has no page after it.

ranked.description:
Whether `data` is a capped ranking rather than a page.

True when `sort` names a window aggregate (`spend`, `subscription`,
`provisioned`, `tokens`, `requests`). Those keys are sums over the events
inside the selected window rather than stored columns, so they are
answered as the top `limit` and cannot be paged. Widen the window or
raise `limit` to see more; do not expect a cursor.

ConversationProjectView.description:
One project a conversation has been observed working in (ADR 0059).

Membership only: a host-stripped `owner/repo` reduced from
the harness process's git remote, never a path, a prompt, or a transcript.
The set carries no cost columns by design — spend is keyed on the slug
stamped on each inference event, not on the conversation's membership.

repo_ref.description:
Latest branch or short SHA seen for this slug. Branch churn does not
make a new project, so this moves while the row stays.

role.description:
Whether events may be assigned this slug: `allocatable` for the one slug

attribution_quality.description:
`exact` for a server-observed harness identifier, `client_asserted` for
a generic one the client supplied. Traffic grouped under a
`client_asserted` identity is only as trustworthy as the client.

wherever `priced_request_count` is below `inference_requests`.

last_activity_at.description: UTC most-recent activity timestamp, RFC3339. The sort key.

last_turn_credits_cost_microusd.description: Prepaid-credit cost added by the latest user turn, in micro-US-dollars.

last_turn_estimated_cost_microusd.description: Metered cost added by the latest user turn, in micro-US-dollars.

run_count.description: Exact client runs, when the client supplied them.

subscription_cost_microusd.description:

avg_user_message_count.description: Mean user-message count across committed requests that recorded one.

cached_input_tokens.description: Known input tokens served from a provider cache.

credits_cost_microusd.description: Cost drawn from prepaid usage credits, in micro-US-dollars.

events_truncated.description:

true, `events` is the 500 most recent and the earlier ones are not in
this response; `inference_requests` still counts the whole conversation.

last_turn_credits_cost_microusd.description: Prepaid-credit cost added by the latest user turn, in micro-US-dollars.

means `repo_slug` names only the most recent of them.

projects.description:
Every project this conversation has been observed in (ADR 0059),
most recently seen first. Empty when nothing was ever observed, which
is the ordinary case for a client that posts no project snapshot.

provisional_request_count.description: Requests with complete rates but approximate provider usage.

repo_slug.description:

A display handle and nothing more: a conversation that resumed in
another clone reports the last one it was seen in, while the events it
recorded earlier keep the slug they were stamped with. Grouping this
conversation's whole cost under this slug is exactly the error ADR 0059
rejects; `projects` lists the full set, and spend by repo is a `listUsage`
question.

oneOf.description:
The conversation's newest live route-affinity pin (ADR 0056), or null
when none holds.

A conversation keeps one pin per gateway model it has used; the newest
is the one its next request is likeliest to ride. `listRouteAffinity`
with `conversation_id` returns all of them, and needs administrator
rights; this field rides the conversation's own access rule instead.

subscription_cost_microusd.description: Cost a user's own subscription absorbed, in micro-US-dollars.

title.description: Generated conversation title, or null until enough user context exists.

unpriceable_request_count.description: Requests with no usable provider token counts.

baseline.description: What it was compared against, in the same unit.

client_name.description:
Authenticating client the finding is about, or null for traffic that
named none.

committed_requests.description:
Committed attempts behind the finding; abandoned failover attempts are
excluded.

first_turn_requests.description: Committed conversation-opening attempts in the window.

gateway_id.description:
Client-visible model ID, as recorded on the events rather than read
from the live catalog, which may have since renamed the row.

impact_microusd.description:
Spend over the window the finding accounts for, in micro-USD. Null
where the saving depends on choosing a different route, which the
gateway does not price.

model_id.description:
Catalog model, or null when the events predate model attribution or the
catalog row has since been deleted.

observed.description:
What this subject does, in the rule's unit: preamble bytes, micro-USD
of cache-write premium, or a share of the context window between 0
and 1.

provider_name.description: Provider display name, likewise recorded on the events.

shape_recorded_requests.description:
Committed attempts that recorded a request shape at all — the
denominator for every shape-derived number here (ADR 0031).

CostFindingsResponse.description: Advisory findings over the window, ranked.

since.description: Inclusive RFC3339 lower bound actually applied, including the default.

subjects_examined.description:
Subjects the window held. No findings over a non-zero subject count is
a clean bill of health; zero subjects means there was nothing to read.

until.description: Exclusive RFC3339 upper bound actually applied.

reconciliation_started.description: Whether events waiting on this multiplier were queued for repricing.

CostMultiplierView.description: One multiplier in force for a model.

geo.description:
Pinned geography for a residency multiplier, `*` for any pinned geography, or null
for a batch or negotiated discount, which is not keyed by geography.

multiplier.description: The factor as a decimal string, e.g. `"1.1"`.

source.description:
Whether an administrator entered this value or the gateway seeded a published one.

A seeded value is a real, applied multiplier rather than a suggestion, and replacing
it is an override rather than a first entry. The console says which it is so nobody
mistakes an inherited number for a decision the installation made.

CostMultipliersResponse.description: Every multiplier in force for one model.

event_count.description: Number of inference events carrying that classification.

CostStateSummaryResponse.description: Cost-state distribution, overall and per model.

by_model.description:
The same counts broken out by model, so unpriced traffic can be
attributed without a second call per model.

finish_reasons.description:
The raw upstream finish reasons behind those states, per model. Rows
are ordered by event count descending and capped; see
`finish_reasons_truncated`.

finish_reasons_truncated.description:
True when the window held more distinct finish-reason groups than the
response carries. The reason is provider-controlled text, so the row
count has no bound a schema can promise; what the cap drops is the
lowest-volume tail. Narrow the window or model filter to see it.

overall.description: Counts across the matched window, one row per `cost_state` observed.

terminal_states.description:
How responses ended, per model. Unlike the `cost_state` counts these do
not partition the window: `terminal_state` is nullable and is never
backfilled, so the null group is reported as its own row and any
aggregate over these counts is over recorded events only.

unpriceable_causes.description: Permanently unpriceable traffic grouped by its content-free failure shape.

effect.description: `deny` subtracts and is never overridden; `allow` is a restrict-to set.

operation.description:
Exact operation identifier from the app's ceiling, `tool:<name>` for
one tool on an MCP app, or `*` on a deny.

scope_id.description: Team, user, or sandbox-profile ID; absent exactly for app scope.

How the gateway authenticates to it.

Fixed by `kind` for `datadog` and `vercel` (`shared_secret`), `sentry`,
`linear`, `figma`, `slack`, `atlassian`, `pagerduty`, and `gitlab`
(`delegated_oauth`); anything sent for those is ignored.
The credential to store, for an app that presents one.

endpoint_url.description:
Origin the gateway calls. Defaults to `https://sentry.io` for `sentry`,
Linear's hosted MCP endpoint for `linear`, and `https://api.figma.com`
for `figma`, which accepts nothing else. Slack's hosted MCP endpoint for
`slack`, Atlassian's hosted Rovo MCP endpoint for `atlassian`,

for `vercel`, which accepts nothing else, and `https://gitlab.com` for
`gitlab`. A self-managed GitLab names its instance here, path prefix
included; every OAuth endpoint is derived from it. Where an origin is
pinned, any other value is refused rather than stored.

oneOf.description:
Streaming git egress, for `git_forge` and `gitlab`. Required for
`git_forge`; `gitlab` fixes its placement and defaults its slug, so the
member is optional there and carries only the bounds.
Delegated-OAuth client configuration, for a `delegated_oauth` app.

Governed REST projection, for `rest_api`, `datadog`, `sentry`, `linear`,
`figma`, `slack`, `atlassian`, `pagerduty`, and `vercel`.

CreateCostLimitRequest.description:
One cap to create. Scope, traffic split, and window fix which requests the
cap sees and cannot be changed afterwards; the amount and the switch can.

applies_to.description:
Which traffic the cap sees: `all` for every metered request in scope,
`sandbox` for gateway-hosted sandbox spend only. Defaults to `all`.

enabled.description:
Whether the cap is enforced. Defaults to true; a disabled policy is
retained and tracked but never denies a request.

limit_microusd.description:
The cap, in micro-US-dollars: 1 000 000 to the dollar. `0` denies the
scope's metered inference outright rather than meaning "unlimited".

scope_id.description:
The account, team, or gateway model this cap applies to — from
`listPeople`, `listTeams`, or `listProviderModels` respectively. Null
for `installation`, required for every other scope.

scope_type.description:
What the cap covers. `installation` is the whole gateway; every other
value names a target in `scope_id`. `connected_app` is reserved and
refused until inference spend can be attributed to an app.

window.description:
The calendar window spend is accumulated over, in the installation's
configured time zone. One policy per scope, traffic split, and window.

allowed_email_domains.description: Email domains allowed to create accounts; empty means unrestricted.

client_id.description: OAuth client identifier this gateway presents to the issuer.

client_secret.description: OAuth client secret. Write-only: no operation reads it back.

issuer.description: Exact OIDC issuer URL. Must be `https`; it is the trust root.

CreateModelRequest.description:
Request to add a model to the catalog.

Rates are decimal strings, not numbers: binary floating point cannot
represent every rate exactly, and a silently rounded price bills real money
incorrectly.

cached_input_price_per_million.description: Cache-read rate. Omit to bill cached input at the input rate.

canonical_model_id.description:
Canonical model identity: which underlying model this is, independent
of the serving provider. Same charset as `gateway_id`. Omit for the
common single-source case and it defaults to the gateway ID; set it
when a source-qualified gateway ID (`kimi-k3-together`,
`anthropic-us-claude-opus-5`) serves a model another route also serves.

context_window.description:
Context window in tokens.

Leave null when the publisher has not stated one. Do not estimate: this
value is served to clients, which size their own token budgets from it,
and a guess becomes a truncated request. Bedrock and Vertex require it.

fast_cached_input_price_per_million.description: Fast-tier cache-read rate. Omit to bill fast cached input at the fast input rate.

fast_input_price_per_million.description:
Premium-tier input rate, covering Anthropic fast mode and `OpenAI` priority
processing alike. Fast input and output are all-or-nothing, and a fast cache rate
requires a fast input rate: the fast rates never fall back to the standard ones,
because a premium tier costs more and reading across understates it.

fast_output_price_per_million.description: Fast-tier output rate in US dollars per million tokens.

flex_cached_input_price_per_million.description: Flex-tier cache-read rate. Omit to bill flex cached input at the flex input rate.

flex_input_price_per_million.description:
Discount-tier input rate, covering `OpenAI` flex processing. Flex input and output
are all-or-nothing, and a flex cache rate requires a flex input rate: the flex
rates never fall back to the standard ones, because a discount tier costs less and
reading across overstates it.

flex_output_price_per_million.description: Flex-tier output rate in US dollars per million tokens.

gateway_id.description: Identifier clients will request. Lowercase letters, digits, and `._:-`.

input_price_per_million.description:
Input rate in US dollars per million tokens, e.g. `"1.25"`.

Input and output rates are all-or-nothing: supply both or neither. Any
cache rate requires an input rate to fall back to.

long_context_input_threshold.description:
Input token count above which estimates apply the 2× input/cache and
1.5× output long-context surcharge. Omit when the publisher has no such
rule.

max_output_tokens.description: Maximum output tokens per response. Leave null when unstated; never guess.

output_price_per_million.description: Output rate in US dollars per million tokens.

provider_id.description: Provider that will serve this model.

provisioned_capacity_mode.description:
How this route binds requests to provider-provisioned capacity.

Omit this to preserve the provider's ordinary behavior. `provider_observed`
and `metered_only` apply to `OpenAI`; `route_resource` and `metered_only`
apply to Bedrock; `dedicated_only` and `metered_only` apply to Vertex.

supported_reasoning_efforts.description:
Reasoning effort tokens this model's upstream accepts, in any order
and deduplicated on persist. Omit to leave the ladder unstated — the
upstream decides which requests it refuses; pass an empty array to
record that the model takes no effort control.

supports_anthropic_message_batches.description: Whether to expose the model on the Anthropic Message Batches surface.

supports_anthropic_messages.description:
Whether to expose the model on the Anthropic Messages surface.

The provider kind decides which surfaces are legal: Anthropic providers
serve Messages only, `OpenAI` providers serve Responses only, Bedrock may
serve either, and Vertex is decided by the publisher prefix of
`upstream_id`. A combination the provider cannot serve is rejected with
`protocol_contract`.

supports_openai_responses.description: Whether to expose the model on the `OpenAI` Responses surface.

supports_tools.description: Whether the model supports tool calls.

supports_vision.description: Whether the model accepts image input.

ultrafast_cached_input_price_per_million.description: Ultrafast-tier cache-read rate. Omit to use the Ultrafast input rate.

ultrafast_input_price_per_million.description:
Contract input rate for `OpenAI` Ultrafast processing. Ultrafast input and output
are all-or-nothing, and an Ultrafast cache rate requires an Ultrafast input rate.
These rates never fall back to Fast or Standard because `OpenAI` publishes no
public equivalence for this access-controlled tier.

ultrafast_output_price_per_million.description: Ultrafast-tier output rate in US dollars per million tokens.

display_name.description: Display name, when one is wanted.

email.description: Email address, unique across the installation.

password.description: Local password. Required for `password`, rejected for `sso`.

username.description: Local username. Required for `password`, rejected for `sso`.

CreateProviderRequest.description:
Request to configure a new model provider.

Which fields are required depends on `provider_kind` and `cloud_identity_mode`;
a field the selected combination does not use must be left out rather than
sent empty. Rejections name the rule and the field, so correct that field
rather than varying the others.

api_key.description:
Provider API key, required when `auth_method` is `api_key`.

Encrypted before storage and never returned by any read.

auth_method.description:
How the gateway authenticates to it.

Bedrock and Vertex accept only `workload_identity`. Anthropic and
`OpenAI`-shaped providers accept `api_key`, or `none` when the provider
is served entirely by subscription credentials.

oneOf.description:
How the gateway obtains cloud credentials, required for Bedrock and
Vertex. `default_chain` and `assume_role` are AWS; `application_default`
and `service_account_impersonation` are Google.

endpoint_url.description: Override for the upstream base URL. Absolute HTTPS, no path or query.

external_id.description: External ID matching the assumed role's trust policy, if it sets one.

gcp_project_id.description: Google Cloud project, required for Vertex.

gcp_quota_project_id.description: Google Cloud project billed for quota, if different.

gcp_service_account_email.description:
Service account to impersonate, required by and only by
`service_account_impersonation`.

mantle_project_id.description:
Bedrock project this provider routes through. Defaults to `default`.

An installation that pins its approved projects rejects any other value
with `bedrock_project_not_approved`.

oneOf.description: Bedrock data-retention policy. Defaults to `none`, meaning no retention.

Which `OpenAI` API the endpoint serves. `openai_compatible` only.

Defaults to `responses`, which the gateway forwards untouched. Declare
`chat_completions` for an endpoint that serves only that API — xAI,
Together, Mistral, and `DeepSeek` among them — and the gateway translates
the request and the reply. Sent for any other kind it is rejected with
`openai_api_unsupported` rather than stored and never applied.

provider_kind.description: Which upstream this provider talks to.

region.description:
Cloud region, required for Bedrock and Vertex.

On an installation that pins its Bedrock projects, this is taken from the
approved project rather than from the request.

role_arn.description: Role to assume, required by and only by `assume_role`.

CreateRateLimitRequest.description:
One policy to create. Scope and dimension fix which requests the policy
sees and cannot be changed afterwards; the value and the switch can.

dimension.description:
The quantity limited, which also fixes the unit of `limit_value`:
requests in flight for `concurrency`, per-minute rates for
`requests_per_minute` and `tokens_per_minute`. One policy per scope and
dimension.

enabled.description:
Whether the policy is enforced. Defaults to true; a disabled policy is
retained but admits everything.

limit_value.description:
The cap, in the unit `dimension` names. `0` denies every request in
scope on that dimension rather than meaning "unlimited".

scope_id.description:
The account, team, or gateway model this policy applies to — from
`listPeople`, `listTeams`, or `listProviderModels` respectively. Null
for `installation`, required for every other scope.

scope_type.description:
What the policy covers. `installation` is the whole gateway; every other
value names a target in `scope_id`. `connected_app` is reserved and
refused until inference can be attributed to an app.

connector_connection_ids.description: Connector-terminated connections this profile may use.

cpu_limit_millicores.description: CPU ceiling in millicores, at least the request.

default_runner_class.description:
The class a spawn gets when it names none; must be listed in
`runner_classes`. Required exactly when that list is non-empty.

egress_bundles.description:
Egress bundles this profile references, each required (always in the
effective set) or optional (a spawn may add it by name).

foreground_idle_timeout_seconds.description:
Seconds of inactivity while the client remains in the foreground. Omit to
keep the ordinary idle timer.

idle_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds of inactivity before the sandbox is stopped, 60 to 86400.

image.description: Digest-pinned workload image, ending `@sha256:` and 64 hex characters.

max_pod_incarnations.description:
Pod incarnations one sandbox may consume, 1 to 16. Defaults to 3;
1 disables reincarnation after infrastructure loss (ADR 0068 part 3).

memory_limit_mib.description: Memory ceiling in MiB, at least the request.

name.description:
Slug-shaped name clients will select by: 1 to 63 lowercase letters,
digits, and dashes, not starting with a dash.

node_selector.description: Node placement selector object; omit for no constraint.

permits_repositories.description: Whether a spawn may declare a pinned repository. Off by default.

permitted_harnesses.description: Harnesses this profile permits. At least one.

permitted_model_routes.description:
Gateway model IDs this profile permits. Empty — the default — declares
no model restriction, so every existing caller keeps its behavior.

pod_annotations.description:
Annotations rendered onto this profile's pods; omit for none.

A JSON object of string keys and string values. This is where a
provisioner's "do not disrupt this node" annotation goes: a sandbox pod
carries `restartPolicy: Never`, so a node consolidated out from under a
running sandbox ends that run for good.

profile_runtime.description: How the workload is started. Defaults to `first_party`.

runner_classes.description:
Runner classes this profile permits, by catalogue name (ADR 0109).
Empty keeps the profile on its own inline size, and `default_runner_class`
must be omitted with it.

runtime_class.description: Hardened runtime class the pod runs under.

spend_ceiling_microusd.description: Per-sandbox ceiling in micro-US-dollars of shadow model cost (all billing classes).

tolerations.description:
Taints this profile's pods tolerate; omit to tolerate none.

A JSON array of Kubernetes tolerations, each naming the taint `key` it
tolerates and an `operator` of `Exists` or `Equal`. A dedicated node
pool for a hardened runtime is normally tainted, so a profile with no
toleration is one the scheduler will never place there.

tunnel_domains.description:
Exact-match tunnel domains, as bare strings (blind, the original
contract) or `{domain, mode}` objects. Empty by default, and empty is
the safe value.

wall_clock_timeout_seconds.description: Total seconds a sandbox may live, at least the idle timeout.

warm_image_reference.description: Repository reference whose warm layer to refresh. Omit for cold starts.

warm_image_schedule.description:
Schedule for refreshing the warm image. Required with the reference, and
refused without it.

DeletedConnectedAppView.description:
A connected app a delete left behind.

Deleting an app is a soft delete: the row stays so the recorded calls made
through it keep resolving to something. What it no longer holds is its
identifiers — a deleted app's name and tool slug are free for a new app to
take. This view exists so that the rows a soft delete leaves are visible at
all, since `listConnectedApps` cannot show them without meaning something
different by "connected app".

held_by.description: What still references the app, and how much of it.

id.description: Stable app ID, and what a purge names.

name.description: The name it carried when it was deleted.

purgeable.description:
Whether `purgeConnectedApp` would succeed right now — nothing recorded
or configured references the app.

Precomputed here so a caller can tell a purgeable row from a retained
one without attempting the purge. A snapshot, not a reservation: the
purge re-counts under a lock and remains the authority, so a purge can
still be refused if a reference lands between this read and the call.

tool_slug.description: The slug it exposed tools under, when it had a projection.

DirectEndpointResolution.description: What to do with Direct MCP endpoints a policy change would strand.

DiscoveredModelView.description:
One model the upstream reported, normalized across provider kinds.

Bedrock and Vertex describe their catalogs differently, and an agent asking
"what can I import" should not have to branch on which cloud answered. The
fields kept are the ones [`CreateModelRequest`] needs; everything the admin
page uses for presentation is left out.

access_detail.description: What to do about `access_state`, in prose.

access_state.description:
Stable slug for why the model is or is not usable.

`ready` for a model that can serve now. The rest name what is missing:
Bedrock reports `adapter_review`, `profile_required`, `retention_setup`,
`retention_blocked`, `policy_blocked`, `action_required`, `unverified`,
and `inactive`; Vertex reports `action_required` and `location_required`.

context_window.description:
Context window in tokens, or null when the upstream does not state one.

Bedrock's model listing carries no limits, so this is null for every
Bedrock model. Null means unknown, not unlimited: look the value up in
the publisher's documentation rather than estimating it, because clients
size their token budgets from what the catalog serves.

importable.description:
Whether this model can be added to the catalog as it stands.

False means something about the account, not the request, has to change
first — see `access_state`. Creating the model anyway is not blocked, but
it will not serve traffic.

lifecycle.description: Publisher lifecycle stage, verbatim from the upstream.

max_output_tokens.description: Maximum output tokens per response, null when unstated. Never estimate.

published_cache_pricing_detail.description: Why cache dimensions remain absent when standard rates resolved.

published_cache_write_1h_price_per_milli.description: Published one-hour cache-write rate, when exactly identified.

published_cache_write_5m_price_per_milli.description: Published five-minute cache-write rate, when exactly identified.

published_cached_input_price_per_million.description: Published cache-read rate, when AWS exposes an exact matching dimension.

published_input_price_per_million.description:
Published input rate in US dollars per million tokens, when the upstream
publishes one for this model in this region.

Present for Bedrock models the gateway holds a published rate for, null
everywhere else. It is the vendor's list price, not the installation's
negotiated rate, and it is offered so that `createProviderModel` can be
called with a real figure rather than an invented one — not as a value to
pass through unread.

published_output_price_per_million.description: Published output rate, on the same terms as the input rate.

published_price_effective_date.description: Date the published rates were last confirmed, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

published_scheduled_price_effective_date.description: Future AWS price boundary, when the Price List already publishes one.

suggested_canonical_model_id.description:
Which underlying model this is, independent of the serving route or
speed tier. Set when the upstream has a source-qualified variant (e.g.
a Fireworks fast router) that shares an identity with another model.
Null means the gateway ID itself is the canonical identity.

suggested_gateway_id.description:
Vendor-first gateway ID the gateway suggests for this model.

Only a suggestion, but a considered one: Claude Code silently drops
discovered models whose ID starts with neither `claude` nor `anthropic`,
so a name chosen freehand can leave the model invisible in that client's
picker.

suggested_reasoning_efforts.description:
Reasoning effort tokens the gateway's published-ladder table records
for this model's canonical identity. Null means no published ladder —
the field is a prefill for the create form, never an upstream fact.

supports_vision.description: Whether the model accepts image input.

One operator-owned egress bundle: a named set of `(domain, mode)` entries
(ADR 0109, modes per ADR 0072).

name.description: Slug-shaped name profiles and spawns select by.

profile_names.description: Live profiles currently referencing this bundle, by name.

removed_endpoint_ids.description: Direct endpoints the app was removed from.

switched_endpoint_ids.description: Endpoints moved from Direct to Gateway-Attested.

EngineKind.description:
The code-owned implementations an engine instance can name.

A closed enum rather than a free string so an unrecognized kind is refused
by name at the API boundary instead of reaching storage and becoming a row
that only fails when a request is admitted. Every kind here is in-process;
the external kinds the schema reserves (`webhook`, the managed adapters)
keep their ADR 0055 sequencing and are absent by name until they land.

Estimated metered spend prompt caching avoided, in micro-US-dollars.
Same contract as the by-user rollup: billed rows only, floored,

Whether managed models derive a waterfall from the enabled routes
sharing their canonical model ID — direct providers first, then
hyperscalers, then aggregators. Off, a managed model serves from its
own route only.

trigger_on_rate_limit.description:
The trigger every derived waterfall fails over on. False, the default,
fails over only on outages.

updated_at.description: When the setting last changed, RFC 3339.

field.description: Request field the rule applies to, in JSON pointer-free dotted form.

GatewayClient.description: Authenticated client identity attached to gateway activity.

GitForgeConnectionInput.description:
The git egress and kind-declared REST channel a forge is brokered through.

Deliberately not a variation of [`RestApiConnectionInput`]. A forge carries
no operation catalog — git's protocol endpoints are declared in code, so
there is nothing here for an administrator to widen — and no injection
header, because git authenticates with `Authorization`. The agent access
mode applies to the compiled buffered REST channel only. Its ceilings bound
a streamed packfile and are correspondingly wider; a bound outside its
range is refused, never narrowed to fit.

oneOf.description:
Which agent interfaces expose the compiled REST channel. Defaults to
`both`. Repository git transport remains independent of this choice.

allow_private_networks.description: Whether the forge origin may resolve to a private-network address.

oneOf.description:
Where this forge's push credential comes from. Defaults to `static_token`.

`static_token` stores the token supplied in `credential` and injects it
verbatim, which is the only option for a non-GitHub forge and for an
installation that cannot reach github.com. `github_app` stores a GitHub
App identity instead and mints an hour-long installation token per use,
which leaves no long-lived push credential anywhere. `github_app`
requires `authorization_basic`: a minted token has exactly one
presentation.

Where the stored credential is injected: `authorization_basic` or
`authorization_bearer`. There is no unauthenticated forge.

github_app_id.description:
Non-secret identifier of the GitHub App to mint from.

For `github_app` mode only, and optional there: supply it alongside a
private key when the app already exists, or leave both out and let the
console create the app on GitHub. Refused in `static_token` mode.

max_request_bytes.description: Largest streamed request body in bytes, 1024 to 68719476736. Defaults to 2147483648.

max_response_bytes.description: Largest streamed response body in bytes, 1024 to 68719476736. Defaults to 2147483648.

timeout_seconds.description: End-to-end timeout in seconds, 1 to 3600. Defaults to 900.

tool_slug.description: Slug the runtime egress route addresses the forge by. Unique across apps.

GitForgeCredentialMode.description:
Where one git-forge app's push credential comes from.

The distinction is lifecycle, not transport: both modes reach the forge
as an HTTP basic credential over git smart HTTP, and the sidecar, the pod,
and the wire format are identical either way. What differs is whether the
installation stores a credential a human created and must remember to
rotate, or an identity the gateway mints an hour-long credential from on
each use.

GitForgeGithubAppInstallationListRespons.description: Listing of a forge's approved installations.

data.description: Every installation the forge reported, empty before anyone approves one.

GitForgeGithubAppInstallationView.description: One approved installation of a forge's GitHub App.

account_login.description: Account the app is installed on.

id.description: Identifier a token would be minted for.

repository_selection.description: Whether the install covers every repository or a chosen set.

GitForgeGithubAppPermissionView.description: One requested permission an installation has not accepted.

granted.description: The level the installation carries, absent when it carries none.

name.description: GitHub's own name for the permission.

required.description: The level this gateway's manifest asks for.

GitForgeGithubAppView.description:
The GitHub App one git forge mints installation tokens from.

Everything here is public information about the app or non-secret
configuration pointing at it. The private key is represented only by
`credential_configured`, exactly as `credential_configured` on the app view
represents every other stored secret.

credential_configured.description: Whether a signing key is stored for this forge.

github_app_id.description: Non-secret app identifier, absent until the app has been made.

html_url.description: The app's own page on the forge, when the forge was asked.

install_url.description: Page a human approves an installation of this app on.

installation_id.description: Installation the forge mints for, absent until one is chosen.

installation_settings_url.description: Settings page where an owner changes the installation's repository access.

last_minted_at.description:
When this gateway process last minted a token, if it has.

Per-process: minted tokens live in memory and are never stored, so a
replica that has not minted since it started reports nothing. Absent is
"no evidence here", never "broken".

name.description: Administrator-facing app name, when the forge was asked.

permissions_observed.description:
Whether the installation's accepted permissions could be read at all.

False means the question went unasked — no installation chosen, no
signing key, or the forge was unreachable — and `unmet_permissions`
below says nothing. It is deliberately not conflated with an empty
unmet list, which is the positive answer that the installation is
current.

permissions_update_url.description: Page an owner accepts the new permissions on, when one can be addressed.

slug.description: Slug the app's pages are addressed by.

unmet_permissions.description:
Permissions the manifest asks for that this installation does not carry.

Non-empty is the expected state after a release widens the manifest, not
a fault: a manifest edit cannot grow an App that already exists
(ADR 0052), so the grant only moves when an owner re-approves.

GitForgeGrantSource.description:
How one principal reaches a git-forge app, for the one-per-origin choice.

Reachability is a union, but where exactly one forge app must serve an
origin (a repository spawn, a hosted-machine credential mint) the
directly granted app outranks every team-inherited one, and ambiguity
is judged only among the top rank (ADR 0107 decision 3). A person is
always `team`; only a service identity can hold an app directly.

GitForgeInstallationRepositoryListRespon.description: Listing of repositories the forge installation covers.

data.description: First page of repositories the installation token can see.

GitForgeInstallationRepositoryView.description: One repository the installation token can see.

private.description: Whether the forge treats the repository as private.

GitForgeLogin.description:
Convention the login half of a `git_http_basic` credential follows.

Forges key a token's meaning off the login it arrives with, and the
conventions are few and fixed: GitHub reads `x-access-token` as "the
password is an App installation or fine-grained token", GitLab reads
`oauth2` as "the password is an OAuth access token", and a plain bot
login means the password is that account's own token. Naming the
convention rather than accepting free text is what lets a future
credential recipe — one that mints short-lived installation tokens, say —
arrive as a new variant instead of a reinterpretation of whatever
administrators happened to type.

GitForgeWipRefListResponse.description: Listing of sandbox WIP refs on one repository.

data.description: Every admitted `mg-wip/*` ref the forge reported.

GitForgeWipRefView.description: One `mg-wip/*` branch the forge currently holds.

committed_at.description: Committer timestamp of that object, when the forge served a commit.

message.description: First line of the commit message, when the forge served a commit.

sha.description: Object SHA the ref currently names.

GroupedInferenceUsageView.description:
One aggregate keyed by the exact dimensions requested in `group_by`.

Reports the same committed-attempt efficiency statistics as the by-model
and by-client rollups, at whatever grain was asked for, so narrowing a
question to a window, a filter, or a cross-tabulation does not cost the
answer. One denominator differs and is stated rather than left to be
discovered: token and cost sums count every attempt, abandoned failovers
included, while the latency, context, and message statistics count
committed attempts only — `committed_requests` is the denominator for
those.

avg_message_count.description: Mean northbound message count across committed requests that recorded one.

avg_tool_definition_count.description: Mean declared tool-definition count across committed requests that recorded one.

avg_user_message_count.description: Mean user-message count across committed requests that recorded one.

cache_savings_microusd.description:
Estimated metered spend prompt caching avoided, in micro-US-dollars.
Same contract as the by-user rollup: billed rows only, floored,
negative when write premiums exceeded read savings.

cache_write_input_tokens.description: Input tokens written to a provider prompt cache (cache writes).

cached_input_tokens.description: Input tokens served from a provider prompt cache (cache reads).

committed_requests.description:
Committed requests (`attempt_role` is not abandoned) — the denominator
of every statistic below.

first_turn_cache_write_input_tokens.description: Cache-write input tokens on committed first-turn requests.

first_turn_cost_microusd.description:
Estimated billed cost of committed first-turn requests, in
micro-US-dollars.

first_turn_input_tokens.description: Input tokens on committed first-turn requests.

first_turn_requests.description:
Committed first-turn requests: one user message and nothing else in
the transcript beyond the standing instructions block — the opening
request of a conversation, never a tool-loop continuation. What
starting a session costs — system prompt, standing instruction files,
and tool definitions land here with nothing yet amortized.

key.description: Dimension names mapped to recorded values. Historical nulls remain null.

peak_context_utilization.description: Peak input-tokens / context-window across committed requests.

shape_recorded_requests.description:
Committed requests that recorded request-shape counts — the denominator
for the first-turn statistics. History that predates shape capture has
no `user_message_count` and is excluded from them, not counted as zero.

key.description:
Requested scope dimensions mapped to their recorded values. Present
only when `group_by` was requested; a recorded null remains null.

surface.description:
Brokered surface these evaluations ran on: `inference_request`,
`tool_call`, `tool_result`, or `app_egress`.

mode.description: Mode the gateway actually applies on this surface.

surface.description: Brokered surface this mode applies to.

config.description: The instance's configuration document, as stored.

config_revision.description:
Moves whenever `config` changes. The runtime keys its compiled-engine
cache by `(id, config_revision)`, so this is the number that says
whether a running process is still using an older compile.

config_schema_version.description: Schema version the stored `config` was written against.

in_use_by_policy_count.description:
Policies chaining this instance. Delete is refused while this is
nonzero, because the foreign key is `RESTRICT`.

kind.description:
Code-owned implementation this instance runs: `secrets`, `pii`, or
`term_list`. The external kinds the schema reserves appear here only
once their adapters land.

engine_id.description:
Engine instance that produced the group. Null for groups recorded
before verdicts carried an engine id.

group_ceiling_reached.description:
True when this group's engine instance is at its per-instance group
ceiling and has stopped creating new groups. A rule firing uniquely on
every request looks like a busy queue; this says it is a misconfigured
rule instead.

pattern_ignored.description: True when a category or preview-prefix ignore hides this group from Open.

rule_identity.description:
Stable rule identity for a configured kind's finding; null for a
detector kind, whose vocabulary is the gateway's own.

scope_rule_identity.description:
Rule identity this ignore is confined to, or null when it applies
installation-wide.

effective_modes.description:
Effective mode by brokered surface. Every surface enforces the
configured mode; the projection stays so a future surface that lands
without refusal semantics can say so here.

oneOf.description:
Set when the running catalog has revised the template since. Purely
informational: nothing auto-updates, because an upgrade that silently
changed what a policy flags or blocks is what monitor-by-default exists
to prevent. The upgrade path is to apply the revision alongside, watch
it in monitor mode, and retire this policy.

template_id.description: Catalog entry this policy was applied from, if any.

template_version.description: Catalog version at the time it was applied.

GuardrailTemplateDivergenceView.description:
A template this policy came from that the running catalog has since
revised.

catalog_version.description:
Version the running catalog carries, or null when this build's catalog
no longer carries the entry at all.

GuardrailTemplateEngineView.description: One engine a template composes, as the catalog listing renders it.

engine_key.description: Key this engine would take, without the apply sequence.

rationale.description:
What this engine catches, and what it misses. Read it before promoting
a policy built from this template to enforce.

GuardrailTemplateParameterView.description: A value the template needs before it describes anything.

required.description:
Applying without this is refused rather than creating a policy that
matches nothing.

maturity.description:
`recommended` or `experimental`. An experimental entry is shipped for
evaluation: apply it, read a week of its monitor verdicts, and take its
rationale's evasion model seriously before treating it as a control.

suggested_scope.description:
Where the template usually belongs. A suggestion; the apply request
names the scope it actually uses.

version.description:
Bumped whenever the entry's engines, config, or claims change. An
applied policy records the version it came from, and a later catalog
that moves this number is what a policy's divergence flag reports.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page, or null at the end.

GuardrailVerdictView.description:
One recorded verdict in the cross-request listing.

`findings` carries the category, segment, and offsets of each match plus
the redacted preview. New flagged verdicts also carry the complete
surrounding normalized segment with every detected span redacted.

findings.description: Category, position, and a redacted preview. Never the full secret.

matched_segments.description:
Complete matched segments with every detected span replaced by its
redacted preview, plus highlight offsets into the rendered text.

request_id.description:
Client-visible `x-request-id`, when the surface recorded one. Pass it
to `getInferenceRequest` for the rest of the request's trace.

HostingPresetView.description:
How this installation and this row stand against the add-on's registered
hosting preset.

image_current.description:
True when the row is managed and already runs what install would
declare. False with `pinned` true means a release moved the pin, or
the row was declared by hand, and install updates the workload.

image_digest.description: The digest this deployment pins, for a `first_party` preset with a pin.

image_reference.description:
The image repository install runs from: the pin's, or the one the
tracked releases publish to.

pinned.description:
True when install can run: a pinned image exists, or the preset
tracks releases.

release_repository.description: The GitHub repository a `track_release` preset follows.

data.description: Every provider, whichever authority owns it.

IdentityProviderView.description: A federated sign-in provider, without its client secret.

additional_scopes.description: Scopes requested beyond the built-in OIDC ones.

allowed_email_domains.description: Email domains allowed to create accounts; empty means unrestricted.

jit_enabled.description: Whether an unmatched verified identity may create an account at sign-in.

name.description: Administrator-facing name, shown on the sign-in page.

source.description: Whether deployment configuration or this API owns the provider.

status.description: Whether a verification round trip has succeeded.

scope_rule_identity.description:
Confine the ignore to one rule identity. Omitted, the ignore is
installation-wide, which is what a category ignore usually wants and
what every ignore was before ADR 0066.

ImageProvenanceView.description:
Who built the digest a managed row runs, as a verified attestation
established (ADR 0108).

signer_identity.description:
The signing certificate's identity: the workflow URL and the ref the
run used.

source_repository.description: The GitHub repository the policy required, as `owner/name`.

verified_at.description: When this gateway verified the attestation.

workflow.description: The workflow file the policy required.

user_ids.description: People granted each created model directly, independent of any team.

ImportItemError.description: Why one import item was skipped.

Stable machine-readable rule identifier, the same codes
`createProviderModel` rejects with.

field.description: Request field the rule applies to.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of what to change.

gateway_id.description:
The item's gateway ID as submitted (trimmed), so results can be
correlated without relying on order alone.

oneOf.description:
The created model, populated exactly when `error` is absent. Enabled
state and grant counts reflect the import's work.
